proved_step: Occurrence-2 control lemma. Let G be a loopless cubic multigraph with vertex set V (clauses) and edge set E (variables). Let F_G be the positive CNF with one exactly-one (1-in-3) constraint per vertex on its three incident edges. Then the models of F_G are in bijection with the perfect matchings of G, via T -> T (the set of true edges). Proof: T satisfies the constraint at v iff exactly one edge of T is incident to v; this holds for all v iff T is a perfect matching. Loopless ensures no clause contains the same variable twice. Parallel edges are distinct variables and are handled by the same argument.

proved_step: statement: Parity-support equations for the arity-3 equality signature. Let A=[[a,b],[c,d]] be invertible over C, with columns u=(a,c), v=(b,d). The signature u⊗u⊗u+v⊗v⊗v is supported only on even Hamming weights iff a^3+b^3=0 and ac^2+bd^2=0; it is supported only on odd Hamming weights iff a^2c+b^2d=0 and c^3+d^3=0. Proof: expansion gives coordinates (000,001,010,011,100,101,110,111) equal to (a^3+b^3, a^2c+b^2d, a^2c+b^2d, ac^2+bd^2, a^2c+b^2d, ac^2+bd^2, ac^2+bd^2, c^3+d^3); imposing vanishing on the opposite parity gives precisely those equations.

statement: Every invertible complex matrix A=[[a,b],[c,d]] satisfying the even-support equations a^3+b^3=0 and ac^2+bd^2=0 has the form b=zeta*a, c=eta*d, with a,d nonzero, zeta^3=-1, eta^2=-zeta, and eta!=zeta; conversely every such choice satisfies the equations and is invertible. Proof: if a=0 then b=0 from a^3+b^3=0, contradicting invertibility; likewise b=0 forces a=0. Set zeta=b/a, so zeta^3=-1. The second equation reduces to c^2+zeta*d^2=0. If d=0 then c=0, contradicting invertibility, so set eta=c/d; then eta^2=-zeta. The determinant is ad*(eta-zeta), so invertibility is equivalent to eta!=zeta. Conversely these equations and inequalities directly imply both parity equations and nonzero determinant. This closes only the parameter-classification subproblem; compatibility with transformed EXACT1_3 remains open.

statement: Let A=[[a,b],[c,d]] be invertible over C. If the transformed ternary equality signature is supported only on odd Hamming weights, then the transformed EXACT1_3 signature has nonzero 000 and 111 coordinates and hence is not supported on a single parity class. Proof: odd support gives a^2*c+b^2*d=0 and c^3+d^3=0. The latter plus invertibility forces c,d nonzero. If a=0, then b^2*d=0 forces b=0, contradicting invertibility; similarly b=0 forces a=0. Thus all four entries are nonzero. Under the uniform basis transform, EXACT1_3 is the sum of the three tensors with two copies of u=(a,c) and one copy of v=(b,d), so its 000 coordinate is 3*a^2*b and its 111 coordinate is 3*c^2*d. Both are nonzero over C, while 000 and 111 have opposite parity. This resolves the odd-support branch only; it does not rule out other holographic tractability forms.

statement: Let A=[[a,b],[c,d]] be invertible over C, with columns u=(a,c), v=(b,d). If u^⊗3+v^⊗3 is supported on one parity class, then the transformed EXACT1_3 tensor T=u⊗u⊗v+u⊗v⊗u+v⊗u⊗u is supported on neither parity class. Proof: Even support forces a^3+b^3=0 and ac^2+bd^2=0. The first equation and invertibility imply a,b≠0; the second then implies c,d≠0, since either zero forces the other zero. Odd support forces a^2c+b^2d=0 and c^3+d^3=0. The latter and invertibility imply c,d≠0; the former then implies a,b≠0. In both cases, expansion gives T_000=3a^2b≠0 and T_111=3c^2d≠0. These coordinates have opposite parity, proving the claim. This settles only single-parity compatibility; other holographic tractability forms remain open.
